hypotheses.title: Berberine Extends Drosophila Lifespan via AMPK and Complex I
hypotheses.claim: Berberine extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster by activating AMPK and inhibiting mitochondrial complex I. The longevity effect depends on these two molecular actions.
hypotheses.rationale: AMPK activation improves energy sensing and stress resistance, while mild complex I inhibition can induce beneficial mitohormetic responses that slow aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Berberine-treated flies will live longer than controls, and the extension will be abolished when AMPK or complex I modulation is prevented.
hypotheses.experiment: Administer berberine to flies and compare survival with controls, including AMPK loss-of-function and complex I mutant backgrounds to test dependence of the effect.

hypotheses.title: Green Tea Extract Extends Drosophila Lifespan
hypotheses.claim: Green tea extract extends lifespan in Drosophila melanogaster. Supplementation with the extract increases survival relative to untreated flies.
hypotheses.rationale: Polyphenols in green tea can reduce oxidative stress and modulate nutrient-sensing pathways, both of which are plausible routes to slower aging.
hypotheses.prediction: Flies receiving green tea extract will show significantly longer median and maximum lifespan than untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Supplement the diet of age-synchronized fly cohorts with green tea extract and measure survival curves against matched controls under identical conditions.

hypotheses.rationale: Modulation of conserved signaling pathways by small molecules can alter stress responses and cellular maintenance, potentially producing measurable gains in longevity.

hypotheses.experiment: Administer PNU-74654 in the diet of age-synchronized cohorts and compare survival curves with vehicle-treated controls under identical rearing conditions.
